title: Carlsbad structure: the minority attack and its limits
outcomes: Recognises the app's Carlsbad structure from the pawn squares, and tells it from the look-alike where White still has a c-pawn
Names the usual plans: the b-pawn minority attack, and the e-pawn or kingside play for the other side
Checks that the pawn pushed to b4 is supported before starting the minority attack
Finds a move in this structure without being told the plan, including moves that are not the minority attack

steps.text:
The app's **Carlsbad structure**: one side has pawns on d4 and e3 and no c-pawn, the other has pawns on c6, d5 and e6 (colours may be reversed). This is the app's own definition; books may draw the line differently.
Rule of thumb: with two pawns on the a-, b- and c-files against three, play b2-b4-b5, the **minority attack**, to trade on c6 and leave a pawn to attack.

steps.caption: White to move. White has two pawns on the a-, b- and c-files (a3, b3) against Black's three (a7, b7, c6). One possible line, to show the pawn mechanics: Black can answer differently.

line.say: b4: the a3 pawn guards it, and the engine rates it within 0.4 pawns of its best move.
Black castles. Other replies are possible; this line only shows the pawn mechanics.
b5 attacks the pawn on c6.
Black attacks b5 a second time.
After the exchange Black's c6 pawn is backward: d5 is ahead of it and d4 attacks c5.

claims.statement: Open files: none. Half-open for White: c. Half-open for Black: none.
The pawn on a3 guards b4.
At depth 16 the engine's best move is Bc3; b4 scores within 0.4 pawns of it.
After b4, O-O, b5 the pawn on b5 attacks c6.
After b4, O-O, b5, a6, bxc6, bxc6, Black's pawn on c6 is backward: d5 stands ahead of it and d4 attacks c5.

steps.text: **Rule of thumb, with conditions.** The minority attack tends to work when the exchange on c6 leaves a pawn to attack, rooks can use the c-file, the opponent has no quicker threat, and the pawn you push is not simply lost: count its attackers and defenders first. If one condition fails, a quiet move or the e-pawn break may come first. A weak pawn is a target, not a verdict.

steps.title: Same position, one pawn different
steps.prompt: In the first two positions only White's a-pawn differs (a3 or a2). Predict whether b4 works in each, then check. The third position asks a different question: is it still the Carlsbad structure?

steps.text: **The other side.** With pawns on c6, d5 and e6, the usual plans are the e-pawn break (...e5) and play on the kingside. These are rules of thumb as well. A break is only as good as its support: before ...e5, count what attacks e5 and what defends it, and ask what happens to d5 after dxe5.

steps.prompt: Think about the positions you just played without hints. Before you chose, what did you check? For the side with the minority: was the pawn that goes to b4 supported? For the other side: what attacks and defends the break square? Write one line each.
